🍁The Sunday Spotlight🍁

How Lake-Effect Snow Works
Twenty years ago tomorrow, the October Surprise dropped nearly two feet of heavy, wet snow on Buffalo, 22.6 inches at the airport, with the leaves still on the trees. It was lake-effect snow, the same machine that will start up again in a few weeks. How it works, why it hits some of us and skips others, how forecasters call it, and what the new AI weather models can and can't do about it. An AI wrote this section.
1. The machine. Lake-effect snow starts when very cold air blows across a lake that is still warm. The lake heats and moistens the bottom of that air, the warm, wet air rises, and it dumps its water as snow once it reaches land. The bigger the gap between the lake and the air above it, the harder it snows. That is why the season peaks from mid-November into January: the air has turned cold and the lakes haven't yet. What it means for us: Lake Erie is shallow, so in a cold winter it ices over most of the way by February, and once it does, its lake-effect snow mostly shuts off. That shutoff is less reliable than it used to be: Erie hasn't frozen completely since 1996, ice cover has trended down since the 1970s, and low-ice winters now come every three or four years instead of every seven or eight. In a low-ice winter, Erie can keep making snow for Buffalo and the Southtowns into February and March instead of shutting down in midwinter. In 2024 the lake was essentially ice-free in mid-February; in 2023 it peaked at 11 percent. The swings run both ways, though: the lake was about 95 percent frozen in both 2025 and this past February. Lake Ontario is deep and rarely freezes, so it keeps going all winter.
2. The band. The snow doesn't fall evenly. It comes in long, narrow bands, often 5 to 20 miles wide, that can sit over the same spot for hours. One side of a town can get two feet while the other side sees flurries and sun. Where it lands is all about the wind. A wind from the southwest drives Erie's band toward Buffalo and the Southtowns. A west wind aims it south of Buffalo and into ski country. A northwest wind sends it along the Chautauqua shore, toward Dunkirk. North Tonawanda usually sits north of Erie's bands, which is why it so often gets a dusting while Orchard Park digs out. Lake Ontario's bands mostly run east, toward Oswego and the Tug Hill; Rochester's lakeshore gets them mainly when the wind comes from the north or northwest, and Scottsville, well inland, usually catches the edge of those bands rather than the heart of them.
3. How forecasters call it. The National Weather Service office in Buffalo watches three things: how cold the air is a mile up compared with the lake, which way the wind is blowing, and how long it will keep blowing that way. A small turn in the wind can move a band several miles, which is the difference between a snow day and a normal one. When a band looks likely, the office issues a lake-effect snow watch, then a warning, county by county. What it means for us: a warning for "Erie County" doesn't mean all of Erie County. Read the town list and the timing.
4. What AI changes. This week's hurricane put the new AI forecasting models to a public test, The New York Times reported. Early on, the traditional models, which calculate the weather from the laws of physics, pointed Isaias west toward Alabama and Mississippi; the AI models, trained on decades of past weather, pushed it east toward Pensacola. Through the week the physics models moved toward the AI ones, and the storm came ashore near Destin, about 40 miles east of Pensacola. The Hurricane Center's deputy director told the Times his forecasters don't pick a "winning horse"; they blend the models with human judgment, which often beats any single one. The AI models have now earned trust on where a storm goes, he said, but still trail the physics models on how strong it gets, and both kinds missed Hurricane Otis in 2023, which exploded where there were few weather sensors to feed them.
Why it matters for lake effect. Honestly, it's an open question. Most AI weather models look at the world on a grid of squares roughly 15 miles across, which is about the width of a single lake band, too coarse to say which town gets buried. For the band itself, the Buffalo office still leans on fine-grained physics models and its own forecasters, who know these lakes. Where AI may help is the bigger picture: when the arctic air arrives and how long the wind holds steady. That is half the call. What's next: watch whether the Buffalo office's forecast discussions start citing the AI models this winter; that is the sign they are earning a seat at the table.
Coming down the road. The lakes are still warm from summer, so the first cold blast of the season is the one to watch; that setup is what made the October Surprise. The Weather Glass will flag the first lake-effect watch for any of our three towns, and once the snow starts, the paper adds a season-to-date snow tracker for North Tonawanda.

The log Mom logged one Friday about 4 a.m.; it woke her. In the 12 hours before, pressure was climbing. Days since the last one: Garret 5, Dad 5, Mom 2. October so far: one each.
What the barometer told us. The family's numbers are in: Garret's 40 logged migraines since April 2025, against hourly readings from the Niagara Falls station. The barometer did not predict them. Attacks fell on rising and falling days in the same share as any random day, and the size of the change didn't matter either. We'll keep printing the pressure because you like knowing it, and more entries from more of us could still change the answer, but it is weather, not a warning. What did show: attacks cluster. Nearly half came within three days of the one before, so "days since the last one" is the number that means something. Thank you for logging. ✶The National Wire✶

1

Isaias Update: At Least Four Dead

The storm has killed at least four people in Florida and Alabama, and hundreds of thousands are still without power. It has weakened to a post-tropical storm, and its leftovers are today's rain here.

2

Eight Killed in Erie Shooting

A gunman killed eight people, including two children and a pregnant woman, at a house in Erie, Pa., Friday evening. The gunman is also dead. Police say all but one of the dead, including the gunman, were related.

3

Pope Leo to Have Lung Surgery

The 71-year-old pope will have surgery after a nodule was found on his lung. He said it was caught "at a very early stage."

4

Deadly Strike on Riyadh's Airport

At least 12 people, including one American, were killed and 309 hurt in a strike Saturday on Riyadh's main airport. President Trump is weighing whether to join the fight against the Houthis, Iran's allies in Yemen.

☑The Ballot☑

Twenty-Three Days Out
Governor. A new Marist poll has Kathy Hochul ahead of Bruce Blakeman by 11 points among registered voters statewide, but Blakeman ahead upstate, which is where all three of our towns are. President Trump rallied for Blakeman in Syracuse Friday and went after Hochul. What it means: Hochul is still the clear favorite, with the margin coming from downstate. Also on the statewide ballot: Attorney General Letitia James against Saritha Komatireddy, and Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli against Joseph Hernandez.
NY-26, North Tonawanda. Democrat Tim Kennedy against Republican Dennis Hannon. No public poll; the Cook Political Report still rates it solidly Democratic, meaning it isn't considered in play.
NY-23, Dunkirk. Republican Nick Langworthy against Democrat Aaron Gies. They debated Tuesday in Elmira, where affordability and tariffs led the night. The only polls are the campaigns' own, released two weeks ago: Langworthy's had him up 54 to 33, while Gies's found only 44 percent say Langworthy deserves another term. Campaign polls flatter their side; the district leans Republican.
NY-25, Scottsville. Democrat Joe Morelle, in Congress since 2018, is favored again; no public poll, and Cook rates it solidly Democratic.
The state legislature, North Tonawanda. State Senate, 62nd District: Republican Rob Ortt, the Senate's Republican leader, against Democrat Thomas Arida. Assembly, 145th District, which takes in part of North Tonawanda: an open seat, with Angelo Morinello not running; Republican Becky Wydysh against Democrat Nathan McMurray, who ran for Congress in 2018 and 2020. Also on the North Tonawanda ballot: a yes-or-no question on borrowing up to $18 million to build a community center.
The state legislature, Dunkirk. State Senate, 57th District: Republican incumbent George Borrello against Democrat Victoria Guite, a SUNY Fredonia graduate who opposes huge data centers and wants corporations to pay a little more. Scottsville's legislative races come with next Sunday's full ballot guide.
The national read. President Trump campaigned for Republicans in Tennessee Saturday, with midterm voting less than three weeks away.
What to do now. Register by Oct 24. Next Sunday: everything else on your ballot, town by town.
Early voting Oct 24–Nov 1 · register by Oct 24 · Election Day Nov 3.

Rochester Animal Services and The Rescue Effort are waiving adoption fees today to get more shelter animals into homes. The waiver is for today only.

Silver Creek · Seventy-Five Years

Harry and Joan Suski of Silver Creek celebrate their 75th wedding anniversary Oct. 20. They were married in 1951 at Our Lady of Mount Carmel.

Tonawanda · Car Hits Paula's Donuts

A car crashed into Paula's Donuts on Sheridan Drive Friday evening after a crash involving several vehicles in the Town of Tonawanda.

A New Blade Runner

A new trailer for Blade Runner 2099, shown at New York Comic Con, pairs Hunter Schafer with Michelle Yeoh in a limited series set when replicants have taken over. The team describes it as a detective story.

2

Shane Gillis Hosts SNL Again

His third time as host included an on-air slip in a Dr. Seuss sketch, for which he apologized. Rosalía was the musical guest.

3

Barry Manilow Cancels Vegas Shows

The 83-year-old walked off stage after two songs with bronchitis, days into his return to the Westgate residency. The next shows are canceled.
